- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥ 0.67) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next 3–5 days.  
- When sentiment is strongly negative (≤ -0.33), model often underestimates; adjust upward by 1–2% if price is falling sharply.  
- Model consistently overreacts to recent spikes (e.g., +5%+ in 3–5 days), leading to overshoot; cap forecast at 10–15% above recent peak if sentiment is neutral or slightly positive.  
- If true outcome shows mean reversion (e.g., 3–5 consecutive days below 70) after a spike, reduce forecast by 2–5% for next 7–10 days.  
- For 30-day forecasts, model often fails to capture short-term sentiment-driven reversals; if sentiment shifts from + to - within 5 days, reduce forecast by 3–5% for next 5–7 days.  
- If sentiment history shows repeated +0.50 to +1.00 over 3+ days, model tends to overforecast; apply a 1–2% downward correction for next 7 days.  
- If model forecast is >10% above recent 7-day average and sentiment is neutral or negative, reduce forecast by 5–10% to avoid overcorrection.
